title: Shared Beginning of Three Words
statement: Return the length of the longest **prefix** (beginning) that all three texts `first`, `second` and `third` have in common. If they do not even share their first letter, the answer is `0`. A text may be empty.
constraints: all texts use only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: All three start with `fl`; then the letters differ (o, o, i).
The first letters d, r, c all differ.

hints.nudge: Compare the three texts position by position from the start. When do you have to stop?
hints.pattern: One loop over the positions: stop at the first position where a text has ended or the three letters are not all equal.
hints.pseudocode:
i = 0
while i < len(first) and i < len(second) and i < len(third) and first[i] == second[i] == third[i]: i += 1
return i
hints.walkthrough: The common prefix can be at most as long as the shortest text. Walk from position 0: if all three texts still have a letter at position i, and those three letters are equal, the prefix is at least i + 1 long, so continue; otherwise position i is the first place where the texts differ (or one of them ended), and i is the answer. Do not build substrings and compare them again and again; comparing letters directly is O(length of the prefix) in total.
